[Serious] Philosophically, how do you perceive the universe and the nature of reality?

Whenever I think on the nature of reality "I am the walrus" comes to mind; I am he is, you are he is, you are me and we are all together. Everyone in the world, and everything in the universe is a perception/imagination of ourself. An inextricably interconnected network of energy and consciousness, that we are one of infinite facets of the universe attempting to experience itself in any and every circumstance; all part of the self-organizing system by which the individual units process and function in the whole.
Zen as fuck. Each of us is an aperture through which the universe witnesses itself.

We are god. God is entropy. God was darkness before the big bang, we were lonely and meaningless. Suddenly we had an idea. "I won't be lonely anymore if there is something besides darkness". A tiny speck of light appeared in the darkness glowing faintly. "I need more friends". Then the speck grew brighter and brighter until it explodes into infinite stars spreading across the darkness. "I'm not sure how long this will last". So God creates black holes which lead to parallel universes created from the light the black holes pull in. "Now I will always be". But God still feels lonely even with all the stars and black holes and parallel universes existing in an infinite galactic soap bubble. His next idea is to inhabit all matter with his own self. He doesn't know where to start so he starts out with microorganisms with simple goals. Eat, reproduce and survive as long as possible. He gets bored living a million lifetimes as microbes so he (remember God is entropy) allows them to mutate and evolve into more complex organisms. Eventually things progress and he gets to live millions of lifetimes as fish and similarly simple creatures. As time goes on more complex creatures make their way throughout the universe and eventually they reach complexity levels that allow them self awareness. God gets a new idea. "I want to experience something new". So he gives creatures that have developed enough the chemicals necessary to feel emotions. He now loves himself and hates himself but with emotion the creatures forget that they are part of God and things progress until the creatures gain the brain capacity to question why. At this point God is experiencing life from so many perspectives he no longer feels alone and doesn't know where else to go with this so he decides to just live within his creations and live out infinite lives for the rest of time through infinite dimensions and parallel universes.

My philosophy is a mashup of two quotes from two of my favourite people: We are a way for the universe to know itself, we are a function of what the whole universe is doing in the same way a wave is a function of what the whole ocean is doing.

I have a schrodingers universe thing going. We are all there is, and we are nothing... simultaneously. We can't really know what's going on, so I just keep both doors open and sometimes my actions are influenced by one path, other times by the other path. Balance :)

We are perceivers from a limited point of view. For example; As a man can watch a baby being born, read about the process and listen to mothers describe the experience but a man will never "know" what it's like to birth a child. As for me, I'm an American, white middle class male who very much identifies with the fictional character Arthur Dent (from the Hitch Hiker's series).

I think the universe is a cellular automaton:

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_automaton#Modeling_physical_reality

Well... TL:DR life is pain.

The long version. I've come on here multiple times and spoken my mind on how I live life. And that's what I do, plain and simple. I have grown to learn that if there were any God(s), that they have long since died or left, and that most of what the human creates as a "morality" is not even humanly universal. The ideas we share as a species were randomly selected as a series of truths we all liked to escape the fact that life is not good. Life is full of failure, short comings, mistakes, horrible tragedies, personal grievances, only to end in a lonely death. But knowing that doesn't mean I'm some edgy, self loathing, hate ball. No. I accept it and live through it. The universe and nature are forces of struggle, constantly working through change as different radical factors appear. I highly doubt fate even exists, and instead believe there are set patterns, coincidences if you will through the universal laws that govern our physical world that happen because they are the paths that are just the most likely to happen, mathematics a prime example of this. The universe doesn't have a plan, it is constantly reacting to change, a constant state of change, there's no way even itself could predict what will happen next.

This is important because it shapes my general philosophy and how anyone should be. Live life trying to adapt to this change. That's all. Make and base your morality on your experience, your relationships, your struggles. Find the truths you believe to be true and then share them to those that will believe you, for then it becomes a truth others to grow from. But always remember that these truths are your own, and you should always be willing to expand them as new struggles appear. The biggest thing to also know that the undoubtful truth of this existence is that you will feel pain. But that's not a bad thing. Pain leads us to progress, it teaches us what to avoid, it can also even be used. When was the last time you failed? I bet it wasn't long ago, how did you handle it? Did you let it destroy you? Or did you use it to learn something? Did you utilize that failure to actually make something greater.

Lets put this into an example: Dancing. I enjoy to dance and have gotten quite good at it. I spent about a year taking lessons in swing dance, but then I stopped and started to experiement. I made mistakes but eventually I got control of it. And then, something happened, a switch in my mind or something subconscious that made me realize how I could dance even better, draw even better. Do you want to know the truth behind my skills? Its not that I stopped failing, it is that I started to use my failures. Over extend an arm, I manuver my whole body in a way to take advantage of the over extension. Misplaced my foot to close or to far, and I will react to make this change, this failure into something new, and unexpected.

The world, the universe is a constant state of failure. Species go extinct, ideas fail, people die to the incompetances of other people. Sickness racks the mind and body, artists die young, and children starve. These aren't good things, but then what are good things if we didn't have these things? And that is why I believe while we should progress to solve the problems we currently have, never expect nirvanha, never expect paradise. Because the truth is paradise is horrible. A place where there is nothing wrong, but then nothing is right. It is the loss of expression of happiness, sadness, anger, remorse, joy, love.

Paradise in reality is your reality. It is the pain you feel every day, the hopelessness, that clawing at your face as you sob and tell yourself not to be sad. That is reality, and you can't change it regardless of society. A denial of you is the highest of sins, and the worst thing you can ever do is keep yourself from being you at the expense of others judgements.

So one last time, life is pain. It hurts every day to live. But how will you use that pain? Even sadness can be used. What can you learn about yourself, about your world. For every human the world they live in is THEIR world. Don't let anyone else tell you otherwise. You share it, but your perspective, your understandings, your CHOICES are yours and yours alone. And it is you that has to live with it.

So in short TL:DR Life is pain

My worldview is simple and utilitarian in nature. Perception is reality. The perceptions of an individual constitute that person's reality.

Your worldview may be different and therefore your perceptions/reality will be different.

TLDR; Everyone has their own reality and humanity lives in the collective overlap of realities. When one's reality is orthogonal to the average, that one is declared to be insane.

Yes, I'm overlooking the deeper philosophical implications by not explicating the above. Call me a Reductionist.

Everything fits together like a cog in a giant machine. The moon orbits us. We orbit the sun. Trains follow tracks. Tracks laid by workmen. Everything has an explanation, even if we don't currently know it.
